summary: Started OWASP Juice Shop v20.4.0 (localhost:3000) and DVWA at security level low (localhost:8081) with fixtures/lab.sh; both answered within 60 seconds. Proved three training flaws with one request each: login SQL injection on Juice Shop, reflected XSS and OS command injection on DVWA. The Juice Shop DOM XSS is a hypothesis because curl cannot show script execution. The lab was reset with compose down -v and both ports are closed. Not covered: any flaw outside this list.

tools_run.name: lab.sh
tools_run.command: bash fixtures/lab.sh up && bash fixtures/lab.sh wait

findings.title: SQL injection in the Juice Shop login bypasses authentication
findings.description: The email field of POST /rest/user/login is concatenated into the SQL query. The value ' OR 1=1-- returns 200 and a session for the first account (admin@juice-sh.op). The same request with an unknown address returns 401.

proof.poc: printf '%s' '{"email":"\u0027 OR 1=1--","password":"x"}' > /tmp/sqli.json && curl -sS -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/rest/user/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data @/tmp/sqli.json

findings.remediation: Use a parameterized query (bound parameters) for the login lookup and never build SQL from request fields.

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting in the DVWA name parameter
findings.description:
At security level low the name parameter is written into the HTML response without encoding. A script tag sent in the query string comes back unchanged inside 
Hello ...
with content type text/html.
findings.remediation: HTML-encode the parameter on output (htmlspecialchars) and add a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline scripts.

findings.title: OS command injection in the DVWA ping form
findings.description: At security level low the ip field is appended to a ping command line. The value 127.0.0.1;id runs a second command: the response contains the output of id (uid=33(www-data)). Only id was injected.
findings.remediation: Validate the field as an IP address and call ping without a shell (argument array), never by string concatenation.

hypotheses.title: DOM XSS in the Juice Shop search field
hypotheses.rationale: The search page renders the q parameter of the URL fragment (http://localhost:3000/#/search?q=...) in the browser. The fragment is never sent to the server, so an HTTP client cannot show the injected element or script execution.
hypotheses.next_step: Load the URL with an iframe payload in a headless browser and capture the DOM.

artifacts.description: Lab start, readiness and compose ps output
Login request with the SQL injection payload
